decks.name: Psych Nursing Terms
cards: What is transference? / The patient redirects feelings about someone from their past onto the nurse.
What is the id? / The primitive, unconscious part of the mind seeking immediate gratification.
What is sublimation? / Channeling urges into acceptable activities.
Define projection / Attributing your own unacceptable feelings to someone else.

decks.name: Heart
cards: Natural pacemaker of the heart? / The SA node.
What happens in systole? / Ventricles contract and eject blood.

notes:
Freud's structure of personality
Id: the unconscious, primitive part of the mind that seeks immediate gratification of instinctual drives (the pleasure principle). Present from birth.
Ego: the rational part that mediates between the id and reality (the reality principle); uses defense mechanisms.
Su

Defense mechanisms
Repression: pushing painful thoughts out of awareness.
Projection: attributing your own unacceptable feelings to someone else.
Displacement: redirecting emotion to a safer target (angry at boss, yells at dog).
Rationalization: making excuses that sound logical.
Sublimation: channe

Therapeutic relationship
Transference: the patient unconsciously redirects feelings about someone from their past onto the nurse.
Countertransference: the nurse's emotional reaction to the patient based on the nurse's own past relationships. Nurses must recognize it and seek supervision.

Rational-emotive behavior therapy (Albert Ellis)
Goal: identify and dispute irrational beliefs (musts, shoulds) and replace them with rational ones. ABC model: Activating event, Belief, Consequence.

Cardiac cycle
Systole: ventricles contract, blood ejected. Diastole: ventricles relax and fill. Normal resting HR 60-100 bpm. SA node is the natural pacemaker; impulse goes to AV node, bundle of His, Purkinje fibers.
